t.7.100.1: Having gone a yojana and a half, the delight of the Raghus beheld the river Sarayū, whose waters are holy, turned toward the west.
t.7.100.2: Then, at that very moment, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, surrounded by all the gods and by the great-souled seers, arrived.
t.7.100.3: He came to the place where Kākutstha stood ready to depart for heaven, surrounded by hundreds of millions of celestial aerial chariots.
t.7.100.4: And a shower of flowers, released by the wind, fell down like a mighty flood.
t.7.100.5: At that time, which was filled with the sound of hundreds of musical instruments and thronged with Gandharvas and Apsarases, Rāma stepped on foot into the waters of the Sarayū.
t.7.100.6: Then Pitāmaha spoke words from the sky: “Come, Viṣṇu, may good fortune be yours! By good luck you have arrived, Rāghava.”
t.7.100.7: Together with your god-like brothers, O greatly splendid one, enter your own body, that Vaiṣṇava form, that eternal ether.
t.7.100.9: You are the inconceivable, mighty, imperishable Being that holds all things together. O greatly radiant one, enter yourself into whatever form you wish.
t.7.100.8: For you, O god, are the refuge of the worlds, and no one truly knows you except Māyā, O large-eyed one, your consort of old.
t.7.100.10: Having heard the words of the Grandsire and having made his resolve, the great-minded one, together with his younger brothers, entered the radiance of Viṣṇu in his own bodily form.
t.7.100.11: Then the deities worshipped the god who had entered into Viṣṇu, as did the Sādhyas and the hosts of Maruts, together with Indra and with Agni at their head.
t.7.100.12: And those hosts of divine Ṛṣis, the Gandharvas and the Apsarases who were there, the Suparṇas, Nāgas and Yakṣas, and the Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas,
t.7.100.13: Everything was joyful and delighted, everything had its heart's desire fulfilled; crying "Well done, well done!", the whole of heaven was freed from all stain.
t.7.100.15: For all these high-minded ones have followed me out of affection; they are devoted to me and deserve to be honored, and they have given up their very selves for my sake.
t.7.100.14: Then the greatly splendid Viṣṇu said to the Grandfather: "O you of excellent vows, you should grant worlds to these multitudes of people."
t.7.100.16: Having heard those words of Viṣṇu, Brahmā, the lord and teacher of the worlds, said: "These who have assembled here will go to the worlds called Sāṃtānika."
t.7.100.17: And whatever creature born among the animals gives up its life in devotion, thinking of Rāma alone, shall dwell in Saṃtāna, a realm endowed with every excellence and lying next to the world of Brahmā.
t.7.100.18: And the monkeys went to their own source of origin, and likewise the bears too.
t.7.100.20: When the Lord of the gods had spoken thus, all of them, having come to Gopratāra, entered the Sarayū, overwhelmed, their eyes full of tears of joy.
t.7.100.19: Those nobly born beings who had issued forth from the gods and others, from the sages, the Nāgas and the Yakṣas, each returned to those very ones from whom they had come.
t.7.100.21: Whatever living being there was that plunged into the water joyfully, each one, casting off its human body, ascended a celestial chariot.
t.7.100.22: Even those born in animal wombs, having reached the waters of the Sarayū, became divine, with heavenly bodies, like radiant gods.
t.7.100.23: Having gone into the waters of the Sarayū, all beings, both stationary and moving, attained the wetting of those waters and went to the world of the gods.
t.7.100.24: The monkeys, bears and rākṣasas, all of them, casting off their bodies in the water, entered that very source among the gods from which each had sprung.
t.7.100.25: Having thus caused all to attain heaven, the Teacher of the worlds, great-minded and rejoicing, went to heaven together with the rejoicing gods.
